To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in Cuba, STH infection was associated with height, but hair zinc was only associated with height for those children who were not STH infected.
in schoolchildren in Cambodia and Cuba, STH infection is associated with reduced height for age and that in Cambodia, S TH infection is associated with zinc concentration.
STH infections were strongly associated with height for-age z-scores in Cuban but not in Cambodian children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between STH infections, zinc status and growth in children in low- and lower-middle-income countries.
the relationship between STH and zinc in child growth.
the relationship between zinc and STH infection and their association with height for-age in two different settings in low and middle-income countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
STH infections have a negative influence on child growth, but that this influence is less than the influence of zinc deficiency.
STH infection and/or zinc deficiency can influence child growth, but that this depends on population characteristics, and that further research is needed to clarify the mechanisms involved.
STH infection is a risk factor for growth stunting in children in Cuba and Cambodia and that STH infection can be a cause for zinc deficiency in children in Cambodia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the relationship of height for age with zinc concentration is not confounded by STH infection, but STH infection is associated with a lower zinc concentration.
the association between height and zinc in STH-infected schoolchildren is not clear and that further studies are needed to understand the mechanisms behind this.
STH infection is a significant risk factor for stunting in Cuban children and zinc status is a significant risk for stunting in Cambodian children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in areas with high STH prevalence, zinc supplementation might have additional benefits on child growth.
in areas with high prevalences of S TH infection and/or zinc deficiency, it is important to take both infections into account in the assessment of child growth.
the relationship between STH infection, zinc status and height is likely to differ between populations, depending on STH species and the prevalence of zinc deficiency.
